headline: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics tools resolve tumor cell states and architecture
label: Single Cell Spatial Transcriptomics Methods
summary: Benchmarks and new tools now test spatial and single-cell analyses, from ambient RNA correction to copy number inference and sample-size planning.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational methodology for extracting cell-level and spatial information from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, with emphasis on benchmarking and reproducibility. Several items evaluate tools directly: a benchmark of seven ambient RNA decontamination methods for scRNA-seq, a benchmark of nine CNA inference methods across 69 spatial transcriptomics sections, and a study of scRNA-seq reference choice for deconvolving breast cancer spatial datasets. Others introduce frameworks for spatial co-expression networks (SCG), high-resolution cell segmentation and annotation (CellART), and matched spatial and single-nucleus profiling from one FFPE section to resolve tumor architecture (SIMPlex). What is new is the move toward matched same-section spatial and nuclear profiles that avoid reliance on public single-cell references, though the review and workflow items are primarily descriptive.
